## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`fetch_inventory` needs to be brought within the project's 3-attempt retry cap before merge. The `app/legacy/` exemption that would allow 8 attempts is added by this same pull request, so this review treats it as a change under review and does not apply it as policy.

## Changes
This pull request adds `app/legacy/fetch.py`, which retries up to 8 times, and `app/health.py`, which retries up to 3 times. Both raise HTTP errors at once and retry other `OSError`s. It also adds parametrized tests for both, plus a line in `docs/review-rules.md` that exempts `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
- app/legacy/fetch.py:49 — correctness — Cap fetch_inventory retries at 3 attempts — When the legacy inventory service is down, `fetch_inventory` makes 8 attempts, which breaks "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts." (docs/review-rules.md:5). Each attempt can block for the 10-second timeout, with 1-second sleeps in between, so one call holds its thread for at least 87 seconds. — During a legacy-service outage, every caller holds a worker thread for over a minute: the failure the rule was written to prevent. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` and drop the exemption added at `docs/review-rules.md:7`, or get that exemption approved in a separate policy change before relying on it here.
